title: Block Placement Queries
summary: On an infinite number line starting at 0, you handle queries to build obstacles and check if blocks can be placed without intersecting them.
statement: On an infinite number line starting at 0, you handle queries to build obstacles and check if blocks can be placed without intersecting them. For a query of type 1, place an obstacle at a specified distance. For a query of type 2, determine if a block of a given size can be placed within a specified range without overlapping any obstacles. Return a boolean array indicating the feasibility of each block placement.
constraints: The number line begins at zero; type-one query [1,x] inserts a new obstacle at positive coordinate x.
Type-two query [2,x,size] asks whether a closed block of the given length fits somewhere in [0,x] without an obstacle strictly inside it.
Return answers only for type-two queries, preserving their order.
hints: An obstacle ends a gap whose length is its coordinate minus the preceding obstacle; a query also has an unfinished trailing gap ending at x.
Maintain obstacles in sorted order and gap lengths in a point-update, prefix-maximum segment tree.
On insert split one gap and update two endpoints; on query max(prefix gaps through predecessor, x-predecessor).
These are exactly all obstacle-free intervals inside [0,x], so their maximum decides whether a block fits.
